questions.explanation: G-strophanthin is also known as ouabain, which upon hydrolysis yields ouabagenin and rhamnose.

questions.question_text: The duration of action of sublingual nitroglycerin tablet is
questions.explanation: Sublingual nitroglycerin has a rapid onset and a short duration of action, typically lasting about 10 to 30 minutes.

questions.question_text: Identify the adrenergic receptor, whose agonists can be missed used by sportsmen for anabolic effects.
questions.explanation: Beta-2 ($\beta_2$) agonists like clenbuterol are sometimes misused by athletes for their anabolic and fat-reducing properties.

questions.question_text: When the urinary pH becomes 8.0, significant increase in the excretion of the drugs takes place
questions.explanation: Aspirin is a weak acid; in an alkaline urine (pH 8.0), it becomes ionized and its renal excretion is significantly increased due to ion trapping.

questions.explanation: These agents are radiocontrast media that share a 2,4,6-triiodobenzoic acid core structure.

questions.question_text: Tranykypromine, a psychonanaleptic and antidepressant drug is synthesized from
questions.explanation: Tranylcypromine synthesis typically involves cyclization starting from precursors like ethyl phenylcyclopropanecarboxylate.

questions.question_text: List of diseases and ailments which a drug may not purport to prevent or cure or make claims to prevent or cure under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rule 1945 is given under
questions.explanation: Schedule J of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules lists diseases and ailments that cannot be prevented or cured by drugs.

questions.question_text: Annatto consists of the dried seeds of Bixa orellana L. Family Bixaceae. The chief constituent is
questions.explanation: Annatto contains carotenoid pigments, specifically bixin and norbixin, located in the resinous aril.

questions.question_text: 'Cresol with soap solution' is a preparation, in which soap is incorporated to

options.B: Improve mutual miscibility of cresol and water by reducing critical solution temperature of Cresol water system
options.C: Sustain the germicidal action of cresol

questions.explanation: Soap acts as an emulsifying agent that lowers the critical solution temperature, making cresol completely miscible with water in all proportions (Lysol).

questions.question_text: When stoichiometric amount of $CaCl_2$ is added to an emulsion stabilized with sodium alginate, it will

options.B: Change the nature from w/o to o/w
options.C: Change the nature from o/w to w/o
options.D: Accelerate the phenomenon of Ostwald ripening

questions.explanation: Calcium ions cross-link sodium alginate to form insoluble calcium alginate, destroying the stabilizing film and causing the emulsion to crack.

questions.question_text: Chlorine and bromine substitution in aromatic compounds
questions.explanation: Heavy atoms like chlorine and bromine promote intersystem crossing due to the heavy atom effect, which quenches fluorescence.

questions.question_text: Solvent programming, also called gradient elution, involves

options.C: Using the mobile phase is unchanged

questions.explanation: Gradient elution or solvent programming refers to continuously changing the mobile phase composition during chromatographic separation.

questions.question_text: Calibration of the cell constant of conductance cell is carried out by using a solution
questions.explanation: Potassium chloride ($KCl$) solutions of known concentration (typically $0.1\text{ M}$ or $1\text{ M}$) are standard reference solutions used to determine the cell constant of a conductivity cell.

questions.question_text: Hybridoma technology is widely used for producing
questions.explanation: Hybridoma technology fuses antibody-producing B cells with myeloma cells to produce large quantities of monoclonal antibodies.

questions.question_text: 'Gene therapy' refers to the process of

options.A: Identifying disease causing genes and activating them for therapeutic benefits
options.B: Increasing the expression levels of the set of genes involved in a given disease in affected cells through selective modulating agents
options.C: Transfer of new genetic material to the cells of an individual for therapeutic benefit
options.D: Removal of the protein corresponding to the disease causing genes from the cells of the affected individual

questions.explanation: Gene therapy involves introducing genetic material into a patient's cells to treat or prevent disease.

questions.question_text: A technician is attempting to sterilize a plug of cotton in hermetically sealed condition in a glass bottle by autoclaving. Which of the following statement is correct

options.A: It should be sterilized at 115-118° C for 30 minutes
options.B: It should be sterilized at 121 to 124° C for 15 minutes at 15 lbs/sq. inch pressure
options.D: It should be autoclaved at 126-129° C with saturated steam for 10 minutes

questions.explanation: Steam cannot penetrate a hermetically sealed glass bottle containing a cotton plug, rendering autoclave sterilization ineffective in this condition.

questions.question_text: Hyperuricaemia is associated with the abnormal metabolism of
questions.explanation: Hyperuricemia (elevated uric acid) results from abnormal purine metabolism, leading to conditions like gout.

questions.question_text: Arillode is

options.A: Warty out-growth from microphyl, eg., castor
options.B: Succulent growth from hilum covering the entire seed, eg., nutmeg
options.C: Outgrowth originating from micropyle and covering the seeds, eg., cardamom

questions.explanation: An arillode (aril) in cardamom is a fleshy outgrowth originating from the region of the micropyle covering the seed.

questions.question_text: Cinnamon consists of the dried inner bark of the shoots of coppiced tree of Cinnamomum zeylanicum Nees. The typical microscopic charaters of the bark are

options.A: Biseriate medullary rays, secretory cavities containing volatile oil and mucilage and few starch grains in cortical parenchyma and calcium oxalate in parenchymatous cells.
options.B: 2-5 layers of cork cells containing oil globules. Presence of schizogenous canal
options.C: Medullary rays multiseriate, the periderm portion cork has both tangentially and radially elongated cells, stone cells present and no phloem fibers
options.D: Exo-foliated cork, non-lignified with 2-4 layers of phellogens. 15-20 rows of phelloderm. Prominent vascular tissue.

questions.explanation: Cinnamon bark microscopy is characterized by biseriate medullary rays, oil/mucilage cavities, starch, and calcium oxalate needles.

questions.question_text: An essential ingredient in the general preparation of plant tissue culture media is
questions.explanation: Carbon source such as sucrose or glucose is an essential ingredient in all plant tissue culture media to provide energy.

questions.question_text: The mefloquine, proguanil and primaquine can be effectively used in diseases produced by
questions.explanation: Mefloquine, proguanil, and primaquine are antimalarial drugs, which are protozoan parasites.

questions.question_text: Identify the receptor which demonstrates the fastest onset of response, when stimulated
questions.explanation: Ionotropic receptors (ligand-gated ion channels) mediate rapid responses within milliseconds.

questions.question_text: One of the following drugs is converted to the corresponding deoxy nucleotide, which shows cytotoxicity
questions.explanation: 5-Fluorouracil is converted intracellularly to active deoxynucleotide metabolites (like FdUMP) that inhibit thymidylate synthase.

questions.explanation: These chemical structures correspond to phylloquinone (Vitamin $K_1$) and menaquinone (Vitamin $K_2$).

questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation of 4-chloroaniline with benzoyl chloride yields the corresponding benzophenone derivative.

questions.explanation: This reaction sequence is part of the synthesis of specific fused heterocyclic systems like quinazoline or benzodiazepine analogs.

questions.question_text: In the preparation of ointments, macrogels are used as used as
questions.explanation: Macrogols (polyethylene glycols) form water-soluble ointment bases.

questions.question_text: An antioxidant commonly used in the formulation of a non-aqueous parenteral preparation is
questions.explanation: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is lipophilic and suitable as an antioxidant for non-aqueous (oily) parenteral preparations.

questions.question_text: Phosphatidic acid and its derivatives from liposomes because

options.A: In a fully hydrated condition, they are conical in shape
options.B: In a fully hydrated condition, they are cylindrical in shape
options.C: They contain only non-polar moieties in their structures
options.D: Their saponification values are unusually low.

questions.explanation: Molecules with inverted cone shapes or specific packing parameters tend to form non-lamellar structures, whereas cylinder shapes form bilayers.

questions.question_text: With regard to the standards for sterile water for injection, IP, the 'residue on evaporation' limit is

options.A: Higher than water for injection, IP
options.B: Lower than water for injection, IP
options.C: Same as that of the water for injection, IP

questions.explanation: 2-Methyl-1-pentene ($CH_2=C(CH_3)CH_2CH_2CH_3$) has 4 chemically non-equivalent sets of protons.

questions.question_text: In HPLC, the analytical performance improves when

options.C: Coarser particles are paired with shorter columns

questions.explanation: Reducing particle diameter in HPLC decreases plate height (improves column efficiency and resolution according to the Van Deemter equation).

questions.question_text: Increase in the extent of conjugation of a double bonded system results in
questions.explanation: Increasing conjugation decreases the HOMO-LUMO gap, shifting absorption to longer wavelengths (bathochromic or red shift).

questions.question_text: Alkaloids derived from ornithine are (P) Cocaine (Q) Colchicine (R) Hyoscyamine (S) Emetine
questions.explanation: Cocaine and hyoscyamine (tropane alkaloids) are derived from ornithine/proline.

questions.question_text: Aloe barbadensis has two of following characters: (P) The drug obtained is white in color and has a bitter taste (Q) The drugs is opaque, yellowish brown to chocolate brown and breaks with a waxy fracture (R) The drug has a pungent odour and is amorphous under the microscope (S) Under in the microscope, acicular crystals are visible.
questions.explanation: Aloe has a characteristic waxy fracture and shows numerous acicular crystals of aloin under the microscope.

questions.question_text: Tacrolimus is a macrolide antibiotic, which bears the following attributes: (P) Produced from Streptomyces hygroscopicus and is chemically related to cyclosporine (Q) Binds with cytoplasmic peptidyl-propyl-isomerase and can be useful in liver and kidney transplant (R) Produced from Streptomyces tsukubaensis and is chemically, unrelated to cyclosporine (S) An inhibitor of pyrimidine synthesis, used in rheumatoid arthritis
questions.explanation: Tacrolimus is produced by Streptomyces tsukubaensis, is chemically unrelated to cyclosporine, binds FKBP (immunophilin), and is used in transplants.

questions.question_text: Metformin acts by two mechanisms: (P) Increasing insulin secretion (Q) Inhibiting a-glucosidase (R) Decreasing hepatic glucose production (S) Increasing insulin action in muscle and fat
questions.explanation: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose production and increases peripheral insulin sensitivity.

questions.question_text: Metabolic oxidation of carbon -nitrogen, carbon oxygen and carbon - sulphur systems principally involves two basic types of bio-transformation processes: (P) Hydroxylation of the a-carbon atom attached directly to the heteroatom (Q) Mixed function oxidase system also oxidizes carbon atom adjacent to carbonyl and imino functions (R) Hydroxylation of the hetero-atom only (S) Microsomal hydroxylation at allylic carbonatom
questions.explanation: Oxidation of C-N, C-O, and C-S systems typically proceeds via alpha-carbon hydroxylation and heteroatom oxidation.

questions.question_text: The silver salt sulphadiaziane, SILVADENE, is an effective topical antimicrobial agent in burns because of its two important attributes: (P) Board spectrum of activity (Q) Active against pseudomonas spp. (R) The salt is only very slightly soluble and its does not penetrate the wall, instead it acts on the structure (S) The salt is highly soluble and hence it is rapidly absorbed
questions.explanation: Silver sulfadiazine is active against Pseudomonas spp. and has low solubility, releasing silver ions slowly at the burn site.

questions.question_text: In the synthesis of chlorpheniramine, two important ingredients required are: (P) 4-chloro benzyl cyanide (Q) 4-chloro pyridine (R) 2-chloro benzyl cyanide (S) 2-chloro pyridine
questions.explanation: Chlorpheniramine synthesis involves 4-chlorophenylacetonitrile and 2-halopyridine derivatives.

questions.question_text: Zeta potential: (P) Is the difference in potential between the surface of the tightly bound layer and the electroneutral region (Q) Is the potential at the solid surface of the suspended particle (R) Can be positive, zero negative (S) Is the electronanotherodynamic potential
questions.explanation: Zeta potential is the electrokinetic potential at the shear plane and can be positive, zero, or negative.

questions.question_text: Two of official standards for uncoated tablets as per IP are: (P) Shape (Q) Friability (R) Disintegration time (S) Uniformity of weight
questions.explanation: Disintegration time and weight uniformity are mandatory official IP quality control standards for uncoated tablets.

questions.question_text: As per schedule 'O' of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules 1945, the minimum Rider walker coefficients for Grade 1 and 3 Black disinfectant fluids are: (P) 18 (Q) 10 (R) 5 (S) 14
questions.explanation: Grade 1 black disinfectant fluids have a minimum Rideal-Walker coefficient of 18, and Grade 3 has a coefficient of 5.

questions.question_text: The IR spectrum of an organic liquid can be taken by placing it between a pair of polished plates made of
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride (NaCl) and Potassium bromide (KBr) plates are transparent to infrared radiation, making them standard materials for IR liquid films.

questions.question_text: In gas choromatography, derivatisation is desirable to
questions.explanation: Derivatization in GC is used to improve thermal stability of polar compounds and enable suitable interaction with the carrier gas or column.

questions.question_text: Neutral thioaliphatic amino acid found in proteins are
questions.explanation: Methionine contains a thioether group and Cysteine contains a thiol group, both being sulfur-containing (thioaliphatic) amino acids.

questions.question_text: Diazoxide, a benzothiazide derivative produces
questions.explanation: Diazoxide acts as a K+ channel opener, causing vasodilation, and inhibits insulin secretion by hyperpolarizing pancreatic beta cells.

questions.question_text: The principle of ELISA is based on these two observations
questions.explanation: ELISA relies on antibodies and antigens attaching to solid supports while retaining immunological activity, and being coupled to enzymes without losing function.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are likely to be good targets for designing antihypertensive drugs?
questions.explanation: H2 histamine receptors are not typical antihypertensive targets, whereas H2 blockers lower acid, but Calcium channel proteins and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors are classic targets for treating high blood pressure.

questions.question_text: The characteristic of the sabin vaccine administered orally for prevention of polio
questions.explanation: The Sabin vaccine (OPV) consists of live attenuated strains and carries a rare risk of reverting to neurovirulence, causing vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis.

questions.question_text: Match Group I with Group II and identify the correct combination for plant mucilages: (P) Cellwall of seed epidermis - (1) Fenugreek, (Q) Endodermis - (2) Senna, (R) Epidermis of leaf - (3) Squill, (S) Special secretory cell - (4) Linseed
questions.explanation: Matching the anatomical origin of mucilages yields cell wall of seed epidermis in linseed (P-4), endodermis in fenugreek (Q-1), etc.

questions.question_text: Match Crude Drugs (Group I) with Chemical nature of chief constituents (Group II): (Q) Ergot - (3) Indole alkaloids, (P) Jaborandi - (1) Imidazole alkaloids, (R) Kurchi - (2) Steroidal compounds, (S) Pterocarpus - (4) Condensed tannins
questions.explanation: Jaborandi contains pilocarpine (imidazole), Ergot contains ergot alkaloids (indole), Kurchi contains steroidal alkaloids, and Pterocarpus contains tannins.

questions.question_text: Match Common reagents used in pharmacognosy (Group I) with Uses (Group II)
questions.explanation: Aqueous chlor-zinc-iodine stains cellulose blue (P-4), Phloroglucinol stains lignin pink/red (Q-2), etc.

questions.question_text: Match Name of enzyme (Group I) with Description (Group II)
questions.explanation: Sutilains are proteolytic enzymes from Bacillus subtilis (P-4), Urokinase from human kidneys (Q-3), Alteplase is rt-PA (R-2), and Bromelains from pineapples (S-1).

questions.question_text: Match Method of purification (Group I) with Effect on water quality (Group II)
questions.explanation: Entrainment preventive distillation yields specific water qualities, reverse oxide removes endotoxins, ion-exchange removes ions.

questions.question_text: Match Drugs (Group I) with Mechanism (Group II)
questions.explanation: Rifabutin inhibits mycobacterial RNA polymerase (P-2), Penciclovir inhibits viral DNA synthesis (Q-1), Imiquimod is an immunomodulator (R-4), and Amprenavir is a protease inhibitor (S-3).

questions.question_text: Match Reponses/Incidents (Group I) with Bioactive substances (Group II)
questions.explanation: False transmitter involves methyldopa (P-2), St. Anthony's fire involves ergot alkaloids (Q-4), triple response involves histamine (R-1), and Straub phenomenon involves morphine (S-3).

questions.question_text: Match Adverse effects (Group I) with Drugs (Group II)
questions.explanation: Reye's syndrome is associated with aspirin (P-3), hypertrichosis with minoxidil (Q-4), grey baby syndrome with chloramphenicol (R-1), and pinpoint pupil with morphine (S-2).

questions.question_text: Match Technique used (Group I) with Analytical method of evaluation (Group II)
questions.explanation: Polarography involves current-potential measurements, Potentiometry involves potential-volume, Conductometry involves conductance-volume, and Amperometry involves current-volume curves.

questions.question_text: Match Type of Radiation (Group I) with Wave length (Group II)
questions.explanation: Radio frequency has wavelengths > 100 mm (P-1), UV is 200-380 nm (Q-4), X-ray is 10 pm-10 nm (R-3), and Mid-IR is 2.5-50 um (S-2).

questions.question_text: Match Spraying reagents used in Chromatographic methods (Group I) with Type of substance (Group II)
questions.explanation: SbCl3 in CHCl3 detects steroids (P-3), bromocresol green detects carboxylic acids (Q-1), aniline phthalate detects sugars (R-4), and 2,4-DNP detects aldehydes/ketones (S-2).

questions.question_text: Match Antibiotics (Group I) with Test organism for microbiological assay IP (Group II)
questions.explanation: Erythromycin uses Micrococcus luteus (P-4), Doxycycline uses Staphylococcus aureus (Q-1), Carbenicillin uses Pseudomonas aeruginosa (R-2), and Amphotericin B uses Saccharomyces cerevisiae (S-3).

questions.question_text: Match Hormone (Group I) with Action (Group II)
questions.explanation: Vasopressin modulates extensive vasodilation/water balance (P-1), Oxytocin responds to suckling reflex (Q-3), etc.

questions.question_text: The alkaloid concentration in coca leaves vary from
